title: Deploy from a Tarball
description: Finish a partial release extraction: unpack site-v2.tar.gz into /var/www/site and verify the files landed.
scenario: Last night's release half-failed: the previous intern extracted /opt/releases/site-v2.tar.gz into /var/www/site but only the css/ directory made it — index.html and js/ are missing and the site is broken. The tarball's entries sit at the top level (index.html, css/, js/), so a clean extraction into the existing directory fixes everything. /var/www is root-owned, so use sudo.
symptoms: The site returns 404 for / — index.html is missing
The release checklist requires index.html, css/ and js/ to exist after deploy
mission: Extract /opt/releases/site-v2.tar.gz into /var/www/site so that index.html, css/style.css and js/app.js all exist, then verify index.html's content survived.

hints.title: List before extracting
hints.content: `tar -tzf file.tar.gz` shows exactly which paths will appear — no surprises about a wrapping top-level directory.

hints.title: -C chooses the destination
hints.content: `tar -xzf archive -C /var/www/site` extracts INTO that directory instead of the current one.

hints.title: sudo for root-owned targets
hints.content: /var/www belongs to root, so writing into it needs `sudo tar …`.

hints.title: Verify the bytes
hints.content: Extraction is only successful if the content is intact: `grep -q '<h1>' /var/www/site/index.html`.
